passage: So you want to know about the time I almost apologised for something I didn't do? Okay. I'm Lalremsiami, and I was fifteen. I told Shalini, my best friend, that I was scared of moving to the hostel, and by Monday two girls in my class were making sympathy faces at me. When I asked her, she said, "I never told anyone. You're overreacting. You always imagine things." She said it so calmly that for one whole evening I thought, maybe I'm going mad? Then I remembered exactly: I'd said it only to her, on the bench near the water tank, and one of the girls had said, "Shalini told us." That night I wrote the day, the time and the words in my notebook. I didn't argue again. I just stopped sharing things with her and stepped back. It wasn't my fault.

qa.q: Where did Lalremsiami tell Shalini about the hostel?
qa.a: Lalremsiami told Shalini on the bench near the water tank.

qa.q: Why did Lalremsiami have self-doubt for an evening?
qa.a: Shalini said calmly that Lalremsiami was overreacting and always imagined things, which made Lalremsiami wonder about going mad.

qa.q: What did Lalremsiami do that helped as protection?
qa.a: Lalremsiami trusted that clear memory, wrote the day, the time and the words in a notebook, and stepped back instead of arguing.

qa.q: Why might Shalini have insisted she told no one?
qa.a: Perhaps she was embarrassed or afraid of being blamed, so she denied it. The passage does not say, so it is only a guess.

grounding: Lalremsiami's friend denies leaking a secret and calls Lalremsiami overreacting, and Lalremsiami trusts that memory, records details and steps back.

passage:
So, Gurleen, you asked why I stopped sitting with Tanvika. Here's what happened. I'm Jasleen, and I'm still a bit shaky about it.
In February I told Tanvika I was going to try out for the school play. Just her. The next day half the class was teasing me about "the future movie star."
I asked her, calmly, "Did you tell people?" She looked shocked. "What? No! You're imagining things. You probably told someone yourself and forgot. You always overreact."
And for a whole week, I believed her. I started apologising to her. For what, I don't even know.
Then I went back to my diary. I'd written it down that evening: Told only T. Didn't tell Mum even. That was the proof, in my own handwriting.
I didn't fight. I just stepped back. I sit with you now. And when I start doubting myself, I read that line again.

qa.q: What did Jasleen tell Tanvika she was going to try out for?
How did Jasleen feel during the week she believed Tanvika?
qa.a: Jasleen felt confused and full of self-doubt, even apologising without knowing why.

qa.q: What helped Jasleen trust her own memory?
qa.a: Jasleen checked the diary entry written that evening, which showed only Tanvika knew, and then stepped back from the friendship.

qa.q: How does Tanvika seem to react when asked about the leak?
qa.a: Tanvika acts shocked and turns it around, calling Jasleen forgetful and overreacting, perhaps to avoid admitting what she did.

grounding: A teen whose friend denies leaking a secret and calls the teen overdramatic trusts a written record and steps back.

passage:
Day one, Tuesday. Zainab told Madhav at the bus stop that her family was moving to a smaller house after her father's shop closed. By Thursday, a classmate asked her if they were "poor now."
Day two, Friday. Zainab asked Madhav directly. He laughed. "Why would I tell anyone? You're making this up. You're always so dramatic, Zainab." She went home and doubted everything. Maybe she had told someone else. Maybe she was overreacting.
That night she wrote it all down in her notebook: the date, the bus stop, the exact words, who asked her on Thursday. Seeing it on paper, the doubt loosened. She knew what she remembered.
Day three, Monday. Zainab didn't argue with Madhav again. She just stopped sitting with him at lunch and told Ammi the whole story that evening. Ammi said, "You remember right. And none of this is your fault."

qa.q: Where did Zainab tell Madhav her secret?
What was Zainab feeling after Madhav called her dramatic?
qa.a: She felt confused and full of doubt, wondering if she was overreacting or had told someone else.

qa.q: What steps helped Zainab trust herself again?
qa.a: She wrote down the details, trusted her own memory, stepped back from Madhav and told Ammi, who reassured her.

qa.q: Why might Madhav deny it and call Zainab dramatic?
qa.a: He may feel guilty or afraid of looking bad, so he denies it and turns the blame on her instead of admitting what he did.

grounding: A teen whose friend denies leaking her secret and calls her dramatic keeps details, trusts her memory and steps back.
